sentences.text: Shri Narendra Nikhare, learned counsel for the applicant.

Shri R.P. Prajapati, learned Panel Lawyer, for the respond Heard on the question of admission.
Record of the Courts below is available.
Revision is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No.16457/2019, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicant-Kailash Jaiswal.

The revision has been preferred under Section 397/401 of the Cr.P.C., b y the applicant/accused against judgment dated 3.8.2019 passed by I Additional Sessions Shahdol, District Shahdol (MP), i n Criminal Appeal No.38/2014, affirming the judgment dated 21.1.2014 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Shahdol (MP), in Cr. Case No.2429/1999, by which the applicant has been convicted for offence under Sections 7(v) read with Sec. 16(1)(a)(ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 6 months and fine of Rs.1000/-, with default stipulation.

The prosecution story is that on 14.9.1999, Food Inspector inspected the grocery shop of accused/applicant and during inspection in the stock, he found 10 packets of 'Lamsa Tea' on which packing date was mentioned as 6/97.
On demand, accused/applicant did not produce valid license for selling out food articles.
Thereafter, case has been registered against the accused/applicant in the concerned Police Station for the aforesaid offence.
Learned counsel for the accused/applicant submits that accused- applicant is in jail since 3.8.2019.
The shop is in the name of his elder brother- Kamlesh Jaiswal.

There are many contradictions,
omissions and improvements in the version of the prosecution witnesses.
There are fair chances to succeed in the case.
Final hearing of this revision will take time.

sentences.text: Therefore, the application filed on behalf of the applicant may be allowed and the period of his remaining jail sentence may be suspended further and his may be released on bail.
Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State has opposed the application.

After hearing rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties, considering the short sentence of accused/applicant, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered opinion that it would be appropriate to suspend the custodial sentence awarded to the applicant and grant bail to him.
Consequently, I.A. No. 16457/2019 is allowed subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited.

The custodial sentence awarded to the applicant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this revision Applicant-Kailash Jaiswal be released from custody subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only), with one surety in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the trial Court.

The applicant shall appear and mark his presence before the trial Court on 20.11.2019 and shall continue to do so on all such future dates,
as may be given by the trial Court in this behalf, during pendency of the matter.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
C.C. as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR SRIVASTAVA) JUDGE A.Praj.
